# docs_audit_report — 2026-11-19

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
I'd close the tab within 20 seconds. The headline starts strong, but by the bottom of the hero I'm hit with unexplained jargon ("FoVer", "repinned from v2 0.9857"), a contradictory MIT-0 vs. Apache 2.0 license, a wall of unanchored benchmark cards with nonsensical progress bars, and a blog section loudly advertising that the project's own AI agents cheated, faked NTK verifiers with regex, and triggered retractions.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Credibility self-sabotage and unanchored/suspect numbers across `#results`, Hero `.stats-bar`, and `#writing` (1.0 TP rate, 60/60 attacks, 0.125 baseline, and four blog posts about cheating/retractions right on the front page).
2. Hard contradictions and broken page structure: MIT-0 in the hero vs. Apache 2.0 in the footer; three conflicting HumanEval pass-rate numbers; mismatched progress-bar widths; and stray `</div>` tags that orphan the 7th capability card outside `.bento-grid`.
3. Pervasive internal jargon and engineering-diary copy (`paper-v6`, `publication gate`, `operator-initiated upload`, `VeriCoT`, `CRANE`, `CCTU`, `HalluGuard v3`, `KV260`, `PREM`) that treats a public landing page like an internal sprint dashboard.

## DETAILED FINDINGS
### Bloat
- Top navigation bar (`<nav>`) — 12 links inside `.nav-links` plus 2 external CTA buttons (14 links total in a single `1200px` flex row) — cap at 5–6 links and move docs/sub-pages under a single "Docs" entry.
- Hero `.stats-bar` — 4 stat blocks plus a 47-word `.r-card` (with unstyled `.r-desc` class) crammed inside the same horizontal flex bar, duplicating the PyPI, HuggingFace, and 0.9131 AUROC info stated two inches above — remove the `.r-card` from `.stats-bar` completely (0 words).
- `#results` — 12 result cards mixing model benchmarks, hardware bring-up, training speedups, and bugfixes with zero sample sizes or context, while offering nothing scannable — cap at 4–6 core user-facing benchmark cards with baselines and links.
- `#features` ("Seven capabilities, one framework") — 7 bento cards (25–69 words each, individually under 120 words), but padded with 2 non-capabilities ("Research operations" and "APIs & portable memory") and 1 orphaned buzzword card ("TTC & PREM") — cut to 4–5 actual verification capabilities.
- `#preprint` `.section-desc` — 86-word dense paragraph about internal CI re-computation and upload status — cap at 35–45 words.
- `#writing` — 7 blog cards (~35–45 words each), with 5 of the 7 clustered on `2026-05-22`/`2026-05-23` covering internal methodology crises — cap at 3 curated introductory/technical posts.

- Hero `.stats-bar` & `.r-card` — `7,760 Experiment runs`, `382 Completed milestones`, `FoVer math step-errors (5-seed)`, `5-seed dual-condition`, `architecture-only 0.8947`, `Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit` — a stranger doesn't know what `FoVer`, "dual-condition", "v2", or "repinned" mean, nor why "382 milestones" matters.

- `#results` (section intro + 12 cards) — `checked-in experiment artifact`, `synthetic-pilot`, `model-generation headline claims`, `publication gate`, `KV260 FPGA`, `Ising sampler live on silicon`, `Ising-guided fuzzing`, `HumanEval-50`, `EstimationVerifier`, `SVAMP`, `FoVer`, `CRANE`, `VeriCoT`, `CoT`, `GSM8K`, `TP rate`, `PRM-BiasBench-style`, `k=5`, `HalluGuard v3`, `0.0pp`, `CCTU` — virtually every card requires insider knowledge of internal component names, datasets, and flags (`k=5`).

- Hero `.r-card` — `"Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit"` — reads like a changelog erratum pasted into the hero.
- `#results` ("Math extraction — VeriCoT equation-style CoT fix") — literally titled as a bugfix commit (`equation-style CoT fix`) rather than a system capability.

### Inconsistencies
- **License conflict**: `<meta name="description">` and Hero `.hero-badge` declare `MIT-0`, while `<footer>` declares `Apache 2.0 License`.
- **Conflicting HumanEval numbers**: `#features` ("Code") and `#results` card 1 claim `+3.0 points` on 164-problem HumanEval; `#results` card 6 claims `66% → 84% (+18pp)` on `HumanEval-50`; `#results` card 8 claims `70% → 85% (+15pp)` on `HumanEval-50` — three different gains and two different baselines (66% vs. 70%) on the same subset with no explanation of which pipeline is the default.
- **FoVer benchmark vs. baseline confusion**: Hero presents `0.9131` AUROC on `FoVer` as the headline benchmark, whereas `#results` card 7 calls `0.125` the `FoVer baseline` on `SVAMP`.
- **Progress bars contradict their own labels in `#results`**:
  - `+3.0 points on pass-rate` renders a `14.6%` bar.
  - `+4.9 points on compliance` renders a `66.7%` bar.
  - `0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings` renders a `95.6%` full green bar (`100 - 4.4`), visually misrepresenting a tiny 4.4% gain as near-100% performance.
  - Boolean/scaling items (`Ising sampler live on silicon`, `2.0× speedup`) render `100%` bars.
- **"Seven capabilities" vs. actual grid**: Heading says `"What you can check / Seven capabilities, one framework"`, but only 4–5 cards are things you can check; furthermore, a stray `</div>` after card 6 kicks the 7th card (`TTC & PREM`) outside `.bento-grid` (extra stray `</div>` tags also appear in Hero, `#problem`, and `#how`, and `#results` is missing a closing `</div>` for `.container`).
- **"Dual Rust + Python/JAX implementation" vs. Quick Start**: Python tab shows high-level LLM math verification (`VerifyRepairPipeline`), while the Rust tab shows low-level `IsingModel`/`LangevinSampler` physics code (with an undefined `&activations` variable) that doesn't verify LLM output at all.
- **"Install and verify in five lines" vs. code block**: The Python quickstart omits `pip install carnot-ebm` and is 10 lines of code (13 with comments/blank lines).
- **Provenance promise vs. cards**: `#results` intro claims `"Every number below is backed by a checked-in experiment artifact"` and `"labeled by provenance"`, yet not a single card links to an artifact, states which LLM or sample size was tested, or labels whether it is live GPU vs. synthetic.

### Missing essentials
- **Clear single-sentence identity**: The hero starts with one ("checks whether an answer is internally consistent — and suggests a fix when it isn't"), then immediately blurs it across FPGA Ising samplers, autonomous research loops, and PREM self-learning, leaving a stranger unsure what the actual product is.
- **Why to trust the numbers**: Zero links to benchmark scripts/artifacts, zero model names or sample sizes on result cards, no published arXiv ID ("pending operator-initiated upload"), and a blog grid full of self-reported cheating/fabrication/retraction stories that destroys outsider confidence.
- **Complete install instructions**: `pip install carnot-ebm` is buried in prose rather than a shell command in `#quickstart`; no Python/JAX/GPU/Z3 prerequisites, no Rust install command (`cargo add`), and no example showing how to connect Claude, GPT, or local Llama despite claiming support for all of them.
- **Unambiguous license**: Cannot determine whether the project is MIT-0 or Apache 2.0.
- **Credible maintainer / community identity**: Only `© 2026 Ian Blenke · Carnot Project` in tiny muted footer text; no affiliation, project governance, contact channel, or explanation of who maintains it (made weirder by third-person "operator" references).

### Fabrication signals
- **`GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0`** (`#results`, VeriCoT card) — literal 1.0 (100%) true-positive rate with no sample size `n`, no false-positive rate, and no dataset split; looks like a 2-example unit test (`1/2 → 2/2`).
- **`k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks`** (`#results`, PRM-BiasBench-style card) — perfect 100% recall on a tiny (`n=60`), self-authored ("-style") attack set with no false-positive rate reported.
- **`Zero false positives`** (`#writing`, "Carnot Dogfooding by the Numbers": `639 experiments self-verified. 65 brace bugs auto-fixed. Zero false positives.`) — 0.0% FPR claimed with no independent ground-truth audit shown.
- **`99.3% of wrong code flagged`** (`#features`, Code card) — near-perfect recall on HumanEval with no false-positive rate (flagging almost everything gets 99.3% recall, and pass-rate only rises +3.0 points).
- **`0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)`** (`#results`, EstimationVerifier card) — a `0.125` AUROC baseline is severely worse than a coin flip (`0.50`), implying a broken/inverted baseline used as a strawman.
- **`2.0× speedup, identical losses`** (`#results`, Two-GPU parallel retrain) — textbook-perfect linear 2-GPU scaling with literally "identical losses" and no hardware, batch size, or tolerance details.
- **`0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings`** (`#results`, HalluGuard v3) — exact zero degradation with no sample size, benchmark name, or confidence interval, paired with a misleading 95.6% green bar.
- **`7,760 Experiment runs` / `382 Completed milestones` / `30,658 Automated tests`** (Hero `.stats-bar`) — suspiciously inflated counts when paired with adjacent blog posts admitting the autonomous loop ran "95-microsecond" fake 30B evaluations and wrapped regex in NTK docstrings.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The opening pitch — Hero H1 ("Catch the reasoning errors your LLM states with total confidence"), the `#problem` section's concrete `47 + 28 = 76` example, and the first three `#how` cards (`Extract → Check → Repair`) — communicates the core value proposition cleanly in plain English.
- The visual design (typography, dark palette, spacing) and the simple 3-line Python `VerifyRepairPipeline` API concept make the tool look inviting before the jargon and internal laundry take over.
